swift-corelibs-foundation's URLSessionTaskMetrics.swift (Apache-2.0) for the shape, and the port's own loader for the values. The getter is the one the SDK's own header names: NSURLSession.h:1415 declares the property `cellular` with `getter=isCellular`, so the selector is -isCellular and not -cellular, and that is what Foundation/NSURLSessionTaskTransactionMetrics+Counts13.m:106 implements, reading the flag -charon_noteInterfaceFlags:expensive:constrained:proxy: stored. Measured in the 6.1.3 build: the class's own method list carries -isCellular and no -cellular.
entries.measured: read through the port's own note call -charon_noteInterfaceFlags:expensive:constrained:proxy:, which charon_metrics_response makes at NSURLSession.m:676 out of SystemConfiguration, the same question the session already asks before it enqueues. It is the port's own reading of the interface, not a value the release reports about a connection. Not watched on a release either: the only level that could is the 6.1.3 emulator, whose [super resume] is the release's own class, and that probe does not exist.

entries.reason: a literal, by design: the release gives nothing to observe it from. 6.1.3 has no API that reports whether a link is expensive or constrained -- those two arrived with iOS 13 and are the *session configuration's* to say, not the connection's to report -- and whether a connection went through a proxy is the release's own NSURLConnection, which does not say. So the port answers NO, which is the value a release without the signal has, and says so here rather than leaving a reader to believe a measurement was taken

entries.source: SDK 16.4 Foundation/NSURLSession.h:1327 and :1343 for the property and its ios(13.0) availability; the port's own search of its tree for an accessor - Foundation/NSURLSessionTaskMetrics.m:21 lists both properties @dynamic and NSURLSessionTaskTransactionMetrics+Counts13.m defines no accessor for either, so each name occurs in that one line and in this row and nowhere else in the package; and the release's own CFNetwork across the ladder, read from the cache index tools/cache-index/build.lua writes: NSURLSessionTaskTransactionMetrics is present from 10.0.1 on, and neither countOfRequestHeaderBytesSent nor countOfResponseHeaderBytesReceived is in any held rung from 10.0.1 to 12.0 - none of the nine armv7s rungs 10.0.1, 10.1.1, 10.2, 10.2.1, 10.3, 10.3.1, 10.3.2, 10.3.3, 10.3.4, nor the arm64 rungs 11.0 and 12.0 - while both first appear at 16.0 (arm64e) and are still there at 18.0 (arm64e)
entries.reason: the data task's transaction is the release's own connection, and its request and response header bytes reach the release's parser and stop there. A stream task cannot stand in for it: it is a raw TCP connection that sends no request and receives no response, so the socket path that closes the other six has no header to count either (facts/Foundation/NSURLSessionStreamTaskSocketMetrics.md, section 4, measures both halves). What the port would have to count to answer it is the header block it composed itself, and CFNetwork's own additions to that block - Host, Connection, User-Agent - are not observable from the port, so the number would differ from the release's rather than match it
entries.effect: below 10.0 - the bands where the port's own NSURLSessionTaskTransactionMetrics is the class in charge - the port's class lists the property @dynamic and defines no accessor for it, so respondsToSelector: answers NO for the getter and an unchecked read raises unrecognized selector. From 10.0 the release's own class is in charge and this row leaves the bands there, because that is where the class stops being the port's. What the release's own class does with the getter is now measured rather than assumed, and the measurement settles it without reading one class's method list: a method in a cache must have its selector name in that cache, in __TEXT,__objc_methname or in a __cstring literal, and neither name is anywhere in the held rungs 10.0.1 through 12.0, so the release cannot answer it there - while both are present at 16.0 and 18.0. So the gap the port leaves is 10.0 to 15.x, and the 13.0 to 15.x part of it is not measurable on this machine: the held ladder has no rung between 12.0 and 16.0

entries.measured: handed to the transaction by the stream task that owns the socket - NSURLSessionStreamTask9.m:271 calls -charon_noteSocketLocalAddress:port:remoteAddress:remotePort:tlsProtocolVersion:cipherSuite:, and a stream task runs no loader, so the loader is not what makes this one. NOT YET OBSERVED. The only level that could observe these is the 6.1.3 emulator, where [super resume] is the release's own class, and that probe does not exist in this series; the host cannot hold it, because the host's NSURLSessionTask carries -resume mangled to -_onqueue_resume and a stream task cannot be run beside the system's in one process at all (tests/backports/host/streammetrics/ says so in its own header and exits 134 by design). The code is in the library and the 6.1.3 link is green; the measurement is not taken, and this line says so where a porter will read it.
